production.note: US model years 2013-2014 for the 5.8-liter, 662-hp car. Start: Ford's release of 15 May 2012 on the '2013 Ford Shelby GT500'. Last: Ford's 2014 Mustang brochure lists the Shelby GT500 at 662 hp (ford-mustang-2014-brochure); the S550 Mustang that followed for 2015 had no GT500. No opened Ford page says in so many words that 2014 was the last model year. The 2007-2012 GT500 (5.4-liter) is a different car.

body.note: Ford's 2013 Mustang brochure lists the Shelby GT500 in its Coupe, Convertible and Glass Roof columns. The standard car is the coupe.

displacementL.note: Ford: '5.8-liter'. No opened Ford page gives a cc or cubic-inch figure, so the rounded litre figure is Ford's own.

drivetrain.note: Front engine, rear-wheel drive; the 2014 brochure lists a '3.31:1 gear ratio with limited-slip rear differential'.

transmission.note: '6-speed manual transmission', the only transmission (2014 brochure: '6-speed manual').

powerHp.note: Ford release, 15 May 2012. Quote: "The 2013 Ford Shelby GT500 is about to go where no Mustang has gone before, with a complete package for everyday drivers and track-day enthusiasts alike, 662 horsepower and top track speeds of more than 200 mph." Ford's 2014 brochure: '662 hp @ 6,500 rpm' (ford-mustang-2014-brochure). Ford's earlier 2013 brochure printed the pre-certification 650 hp; see discrepancies.

weightLb.note: Ford release, 15 May 2012. Quote: "The most powerful engine ever in a North American production car propels the 3,852-pound vehicle to a top track speed of more than 200 mph, yet is exempt from gas-guzzler tax at a projected 15 mpg city, 24 mpg highway". Ford does not name the body there; John Heilig's review of the coupe (The Auto Channel, 25 Nov 2012) gives the same figure in its spec panel: 'Curb Weight: 3,852 lbs.' (theautochannel-heilig-gt500-2013), so the figure is taken as the standard coupe with the six-speed manual. Ford's release does not call 3,852 lb a curb weight or name the body; the coupe-with-manual reading rests on one review's spec panel, so confidence is medium.

discrepancies.reason: Ford's 2013 Mustang brochure was printed with the pre-certification figure ('650 hp @ 6,500 rpm and 600 lb.-ft. of torque'); Ford's May 2012 release and its 2014 brochure give the certified 662 hp.
discrepancies.resolution: 662 hp, Ford's final SAE rating for the 2013 and 2014 cars.
